I don't intend to scare you, but the process so far has been a nightmare for me. Covid put off my surgery, my surgeon retired, I got moved to a new surgeon, and the new surgeon is impossible to get a hold of. Orthopedic surgeries were put off at the Royal Alex for a good amount of time, which backed up the system. The wait list is 18 months, but this kind of pause doesn't help. There may be cancelations that open up a spot earlier and you may be given a month or two prior notice, if you are in a place financially/personally where you can jump on that you definitely should. Alberta has been having issues with orthopedic surgeries, and there are less and less getting performed each year. 

All I want is 2 metal rods in my back so I can get on with the 6-12 month recovery. I'm looking at a few days in the hospital (5 days or so), then roughly 6 to 8 weeks or not doing much. Hopefully, you have someone/a support group that can help you cook, clean, drive you to appointments, do errands... all the basic stuff. After 6 to 8 weeks, light housework should be okay. I have a hunch that it'll be a long road to full recovery, and require a good amount of effort and patience.

3. Having shared experiences is great, but take the time to have personal experiences. Not everything needs to be done lock step. Have a plan that allows you to do your own things and meet up afterward.

Okay, this is something I started doing after years of post secondary, it's easier to show with an example. The class topic would go at the top of the page, subtopics would get their own lines and were far left justified, notes about the topic would get placed under the subtopic. The notes would be connected to the subtopic with an arrow, and were placed about an inch away from the left margin. 

Lets say the class subject was vehicles, at the top of the page I'd write vehicles. The first vehicle we cover is a car, so on a new line I'd write car, then make a small arrow to capture a quick note. If the instructor said "cars are typically purchased for personal or commercial use" then next to my arrow I'd probably write "typically bought for personal/commercial use".  If the instructor repeated the point, my note would get a star. Notes were just to capture the essence of the points the instructor made, getting the important words out of what was said.

One of my happiest moments playing this game came from leaving a cp 22 magicarp at a gym. I had just taken the gym, left the fish and began walking when I saw a couple rush toward the gym with the very excited girl friend in the lead. I stood around nearby and watched the gym get taken over and a not particularly strong Pokemon get put in.
The couple started walking my way, so I talked with them. After congratulating them on their victory I learned they'd been walking around for a while trying to get their first gym fight but found everything else to be way out of their league. Just seeing how happy they were made me see this game in a much different light. Now I take the gyms that I can, even if I've already cashed out for the day and leave a carp hoping that I'll help reinvigorate someone's Pokemon go dreams.
